requirements_summary: Primary requirement: dedicated capacity with a contractual minimum throughput guarantee. Targets: min 2,500 tokens/sec sustained for production chat tier (model: open-llama-13b variant, fp16/4-bit quantized), concurrency cap: 120 active sessions across model pool, burst allowance: up to 2x baseline tokens/sec for a 10-minute window with automatic throttling thereafter. Latency: p95 < 220ms for sub-256-token requests, p99 < 400ms best-effort; on-paper SLO to include measured tail allowances for customer edge. Reserved GPUs: planning 8x A100-eq for baseline, with contractual burst buffer (up to 4 GPUs) billed differently. Required features: prefix/KV cache for conversational reuse, model fallback routing to smaller variant under capacity pressure, token-level cost reporting, audit logs and KMS integrations, data residency in us-east-1. Cost sensitivity: mid-high; wants predictable monthly commit with clearly defined overage bands and credits for underperformance.
notes:
POC summary and negotiation notes:
- Client voice: "We need guaranteed throughput for trading-hours bursts; can't have dropped requests."
- AE notes: procurement cares most about deterministic unit economics and explicit concurrency caps; legal pushing back on SLA credits vs. penalty.
- SE notes: quantified tests show sustained 2.7k tokens/sec with 8 GPUs at 90% pack efficiency on our synthetic; real-world with KV cache improved effective tokens/sec for chat flows by ~18%.
- Network: customer edge adds ~20-30ms; recommend adding 30ms slack to SLOs or colocate a dedicated NAT/peering in customer VPC.
- GPU planning: client prefers reserved GPU pool model (monthly commit) with defined add-on burst credits. Discussed burst policy options:
   * Option A — Soft burst: allow 2x sustained for 10 minutes, auto-throttle; no extra charge for first two bursts/month, then billed per token.
   * Option B — Reserved burst buffer: customer purchases small burst pool (4 GPUs) charged as standby capacity at discounted rate; guaranteed availability.
   * Option C — Pay-as-you-go overage: unlimited bursts but billed at premium.
- Legal asks: include explicit minimum tokens/sec per model family, concurrency ceilings, measurability (logs and trace IDs), and defined remediation (service credits scaled to % of missed SLO).
- Client-specific: heavy reranking during market open (9:30–10:15 ET) requires guaranteed concurrency of 80 sessions with bursts to 160 for 15 min. They want a canary for rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller model with bounded latency increase.
- Quote: initial committed monthly = $55k/month for baseline reserve (incl. 8 GPU pool + console access); expected uplift for burst buffer TBD depending on Option chosen.
- Roadblock: procurement insistence on SLA that excludes third-party network latency — Redwood to propose measurement method (edge-to-inference RTT) and carveouts.
customer_priorities: 1) Deterministic throughput during market hours; 2) Clear pricing for burst behavior; 3) Measurable SLOs with actionable credits; 4) VPC/private tenancy + KMS; 5) Minimal inference variance across deploy modes.
commercial_notes: Draft MSA under review. Procurement requested commitment term options: 12 vs 24 months. Volume discount bands start at $650k ARR. Finance wants capped exposure for burst usage; propose standby pool as compromise.
technical_risks: 1) Edge network jitter causing p99 violations; 2) Model memory causing fragmentation at high concurrency leading to reduced utilization; 3) Fallback model quality regressions for reranking affecting downstream metrics.
